record.paper_title: Major Unsolved Problems in Space Plasma Physics
record.original_question: How should space-plasma models connect the fluid description of inertial-range magnetohydrodynamic turbulence to kinetic physics in the dissipation range, where scales approach the ion Larmor radius or ion skin depth, magnetic reconnection requires at least approximate electron physics, collisionless regions such as the outer heliosphere challenge fluid approximations, and interstellar pickup ions introduce energetically important non-Maxwellian components?

evidence.quote: the dissipation range of the spectrum is poorly studied and poorly understood.

The fluid description used to study inertial range turbulence breaks down as one approaches spatial scales comparable to the ion Larmor radius or ion skin depth and kinetic effects need to be included.
Even at larger scales, fluid descriptions become questionable in regions of space where the plasma becomes collisionless

artifact.category_tag: magnetohydrodynamic turbulence and kinetic plasma coupling
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a magnetized plasma described on large (inertial-range) scales by the equations of magnetohydrodynamics (MHD): for a single-fluid plasma with mass density ρ, velocity field u, magnetic field B, and pressure p, the equations are

  ∂ρ/∂t + ∇·(ρu) = 0,
  ρ(∂u/∂t + u·∇u) = −∇p + (1/μ₀)(∇×B)×B,
  ∂B/∂t = ∇×(u×B) + η∇²B,
  ∇·B = 0,

together with an equation of state. Turbulence in this regime exhibits a power-law inertial-range cascade. At small scales comparable to the ion Larmor radius r_L = v_⊥/Ω_i (with Ω_i = qB/m_i the ion gyrofrequency) or the ion inertial length d_i = c/ω_pi (with ω_pi the ion plasma frequency), the fluid description fails and kinetic effects governed by the Vlasov–Maxwell system

  ∂f_s/∂t + v·∇f_s + (q_s/m_s)(E + v×B)·∇_v f_s = (∂f_s/∂t)_coll,
  ∇×E = −∂B/∂t,  ∇×B = μ₀ J + (1/c²) ∂E/∂t,

become necessary. Additional complications include: (i) magnetic reconnection events that require at least an approximate treatment of electron-scale physics (e.g. electron inertia, pressure-tensor terms, or Hall MHD with electron contributions); (ii) regions such as the outer heliosphere where collisions are negligible, invalidating closure assumptions of fluid models; and (iii) pickup ions (e.g. from charge exchange with interstellar neutrals) that produce non-Maxwellian, energetically dominant distribution components f_pui(v).

Problem. Construct a mathematical model—either as a hybrid fluid–kinetic system, a reduced gyrokinetic/kinetic-MHD model, or a multi-fluid model with appropriate non-Maxwellian closures—that:

  (a) reduces to standard MHD on scales ≫ max(r_L, d_i);
  (b) captures the transition from the inertial range into the dissipation range across scales ∼ r_L and ∼ d_i, predicting the spectral shape and dissipation mechanism in that range;
  (c) admits magnetic reconnection with electron-scale physics retained at least approximately;
  (d) remains valid in collisionless regimes; and
  (e) self-consistently incorporates an energetically significant non-Maxwellian pickup-ion population.

Prove well-posedness of the resulting system in a suitable functional setting, and identify the conserved quantities, dissipation operators, and predicted energy spectra that connect the MHD inertial range to the kinetic dissipation range.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of bridging MHD inertial-range turbulence with kinetic dissipation-range physics in space plasmas remains an active and largely open research area. Recent reviews and modeling efforts (gyrokinetic, hybrid Vlasov, kinetic-MHD, and reduced models) provide partial descriptions in specific regimes, but no unified model satisfying all of the listed requirements is established.

status_evidence.title: Kinetic turbulence in space plasmas (review)
status_evidence.snippet: The transition from MHD turbulence to kinetic scales near ion gyroradius/skin depth and the nature of dissipation remain open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Connecting MHD inertial-range turbulence to kinetic dissipation-range physics is an open research problem.

status_evidence.title: Pickup ions in the outer heliosphere
status_evidence.snippet: Pickup ions form energetically dominant non-Maxwellian components that strongly affect turbulence and dissipation; their self-consistent inclusion in models is still developing.
status_evidence.claim: Incorporating non-Maxwellian pickup-ion components into turbulence models is ongoing work.
